key_insight: Better web agents need targeted practice in reusable skills, not just more tasks. MiniWeb makes these skills measurable in a realistic miniature web, helping reveal why agents fail.
problem_solved: Task success alone hides the interaction skills that web agents struggle with, making it difficult to diagnose weaknesses and prioritize training.
method: Build MiniWeb: 65 interconnected websites spanning 15 domains for realistic navigation, search, and transaction workflows.
Provide 369 human-annotated tasks labeled with 37 reusable interaction primitives organized into 7 skill families.
Evaluate agents at the skill level to identify specific weaknesses beyond overall task completion.
impact: MiniWeb gives AI practitioners a structured way to diagnose web-agent weaknesses and guide targeted training. The supplied abstract is truncated, so quantitative performance findings are not available.
visual_elements: Miniature web map showing interconnected sites across 15 color-coded domains.
Skill hierarchy diagram grouping 37 interaction primitives into 7 families.
Workflow strip illustrating navigation → search → transaction, with skill labels at each step.
Conceptual skill-performance heatmap showing how agent weaknesses could be compared.
paper_title: Back to Basics: A Skill-Centric Approach to Generalist Web Agents
paper_authors: Minh Pham-Dinh, Md Farhan Ishmam, Hernan Yupanqui, Reaz Hassan Joarder, Kenneth Marino
